{{short description|Physicist}}
{{Use British English|date=June 2020}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2020}}
'''John Christopher Dainty''' is a professor who researches [[optical imaging]], [[scattering]] and propagation.<ref name=SiliconRepublic>{{cite web|title=Professor Christopher Dainty, US Optics Society|url=http://www.siliconrepublic.com/careers/appointments/685-professor-christopher|work=Appointments|publisher=Silicon Republic}}</ref> In these areas he has published books: ''Scattering in Volumes and Surfaces'' (1989, co-edited with M Nieto-Vesperinas), ''Laser Speckle and Related Phenomena'' (1975, 2nd Ed. 1984, editor)<ref name="AppliedOptics">{{cite web|title=Prof. Chris Dainty (M.Sc., Ph.D.(Imperial College, London), F.Inst.P.)|url=http://optics.nuigalway.ie/people/chris/chris.html|work=Applied Optics|publisher=NUI Galway|access-date=9 April 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120520062429/http://optics.nuigalway.ie/people/chris/chris.html|archive-date=20 May 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> and ''Image Science'' (1974) which he co-authored with Rodney Shaw.<ref name="Dainty2012">{{cite web|title=May 24, 2012 - Chris Dainty|url=http://www.nesosa.org/meetings/may-24-2012-chris-dainty|work=Adaptive Optics: Past and Future|publisher=New England Section of the Optical Society of America}}{{Dead link|date=July 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> He has co-authored around 170 peer-reviewed papers and some 300 conference presentations.

==Career==
From 1974 to 1978, Dainty was a lecturer in physics at [[Queen Elizabeth College]] of the [[University of London]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Christopher Dainty Elected VP of US Optics Society|url=http://www.photonics.com/Article.aspx?AID=35620|work=News Briefs|publisher=Photonics.com}}</ref> He joined [[the Institute of Optics]] at the [[University of Rochester]] 1978 and the faculty of the Department of Physics and Astronomy in July 1982.<ref name="Dainty2012" /> He became Pilkington Professor of Applied Optics at [[Imperial College]] in January 1984<ref name="IONS">{{cite web|title=Plenary Speakers|url=http://www.ions-project.org/index.php?topic=ions9_plenary|work=IONS-9/Salamanca|publisher=IONS (International Network of OSA Students)}}</ref> and was [[Science and Engineering Research Council|SERC]] Senior Research Fellow for the period October 1987 to September 1992. From October 2001 to September 2002 he was a [[PPARC]] Senior Research Fellow.<ref>{{cite web|title=About the Authors|url=http://www.imaging.org/IST/store/epub.cfm?abstrid=7117|work=Recent Developments in Adaptive Optics|publisher=Imaging.org}}</ref> In October 2002, Professor Dainty moved to The [[National University of Ireland]], Galway, where he is currently chair of applied physics and Science Foundation Ireland PI. He is simultaneously on extended leave from [[Imperial College]].<ref name="IONS" />

Dainty founded an Industrial Associates Scheme at [[Imperial College]]<ref>{{cite web|title=A History of Optics at Imperial College London|url=http://www3.imperial.ac.uk/photonics/about/history/fullhistory|work=Research: Photonics|publisher=Imperial College London}}</ref> and at [[NUI Galway]] has established links with companies in ICT, healthcare and other industries.<ref name="AppliedOptics" />

Dainty is the 1984 recipient of the [[International Commission of Optics Prize]], the 1993 Thomas [[Young Medal and Prize]] (IoP), the 2003 C.E.K. Mees Medal (OSA), the Optics and Photonics Division Prize 2004 (IoP) and the 2017 Robert E. Hopkins Leadership Award (OSA). He is also a [[OSA Fellow|Fellow]] of The [[Optical Society of America]], [[SPIE]], The [[Institute of Physics]] (UK) and The [[European Optical Society]].<ref name="IONS" /> In March 2008 he was elected a Member of the [[Royal Irish Academy]].<ref name=SiliconRepublic />

From 1983 to 1985 he was elected to the board of directors of the [[Optical Society]] (OSA) - 1987–1990 he was elected secretary-general of the ICO, president for the term 1990–1993 and was past president from 1993 to 1996 - and 1994 to 1996 he was elected to the Board of [[SPIE]]. Dainty served on the council of the UK [[Institute of Physics]] (1996–1999). He was a director at large of the OSA for the period 2005–2007 and 2011 president of OSA (past president in 2012).<ref name="IONS" /> He is a member of the [[IEEE]] P2020 Standards Development body for Automotive Imaging.{{citation needed|date=September 2021}}
